Killswitch:

The Curse of the Black Spot seems like it blatantly drawn inspiration from Pirates of the Carribean: Dead Man's Chest, where Sparrow owed Davy Jones his servitude upon the Flying Dutchman in exchange for his Black Pearl for several years, and he was also marked by a black spot.If we take this parallel literally, perhaps La Commodora made some sort of deal along the same lines, for her La Paradoya Magnifica. And when her time was up, she was hunted across the cosmos. Or time.But I'm just wildly speculating, and I'd love for this to be a thing.

 

LA Capitan (and by extension La Comadora) is frustrating for me in terms of timeline.

 

She snuck onto the ship disguised as a boy. To pull that off she would have been… what 10 to 14 years old?

She was effected by the "Void" she fell in, it was in the ocean so maybe an early form of "The Void"? Or but art for the event is on Time Cataclysm, so maybe it is the beginning of the Singularity OblivAeon is creating.

This leads us to "Curse of the Black Spot", the Time Energies effected her, perhaps taking a massive toll on her body perhaps the curse is something else entirely. To cure herself she has a hi-tech compass which seems reminiscent of the compass from Pirates of the Carribean (which pointed to the persons greatest desire). It looks like she's at least 18 but probably older, so it is safe to say this takes place ten years after she gets the ship.

My best guess is that she went to the Nexus of the Void to find a cure for the Black Spot.

After curing herself, or being cured by one of the heroes, we get her in her early piracy career. Perhaps Chiquito is from the Nexus, being the only companion she's had in many years alone. He could have even grabbed a piece of Omnitron-U during the conflict with OblivAeon or the Aeon Men. Correction: Looks like Chiquito appeared in the Final Wasteland on her first trip. This early Captain is defeated and given by Chrono-Ranger to the Elder LA Comodora.

 

She somehow escapes from her older self, gathers her crew, and becomes the Captain we all know from Shattered Timelines.

 

After many years and many defeats she abadons her crew, eventually runs into Chrono-Ranger and hires him to go and grab her younger self. Then after securing her younger self she goes and helps fight OblivAeon and save all of time and space.

 

Alternatively, Black Spot could take place after She is captured and given to the older captain. La Commadora transfers the terrible Black Spot to her younger self, who goes hero while trying to get a cure, then in retalation for how she was treated by herself gathers her crew and becomes the captain we know and despise.

posts.name: metaphysician
posts.cooked:
I've mentioned my theory on another thread, but here goes:

The Void is what existed before creation, and before the Wager.  It is not emptiness, in fact, its the opposite:  it is the primal chaos that contains the infinite possibility of existence.  Its the realm where Gods, capital G, come from, insofar as they can be declared distinct beings from the realm.  It is dangerous, but not because it is evil or hostile:  its just too much for mere mortals to bear.  The more you touch upon the Void, the more you are transformed by it, both in form and perspective.

Under this theory, Oblivaeon is one of the Void-born Gods.  So is Jansa vi Dero, and also whoever else made the Wager, if Jansa isn't that being.  Its also not coincidence that the Wager turned out the way it did, nor is it coincidence that except for Oblivaeon, all the Void-touched individuals are broadly positive influences on the Multiverse.  In essence, the Void "wanted" Creation and the Multiverse to happen.

( To make an analogy, if this were Lord of the Rings, the Void-born gods are the Valar.  Oblivaeon is Melkor/Morgoth.  The Void is Eru. )
